correctness.rationale: For every pi/4<m<pi/2 the exact closure cosine moment gives the closed two-arc, two-segment body. Nonnegative curvature-radius measures and positive gap atoms imply convexity; opposing active widths equal one and complement widths exceed one; C1 support on active normals forces reducedness. Green's formula gives the sine-kernel quadratic area. Any moment-zero even profile difference delta produces a zero-Dirichlet potential z satisfying z''+z=2delta. The Dirichlet Poincare inequality makes the quadratic form strictly negative for nonzero delta. For the explicitly feasible bang-bang profile, the potential divided by cos x is constant centrally and increasing outward, yielding the global first-order support inequality. Strict concavity proves uniqueness; elementary integration yields exact area and potential-norm stability. The embedded exact-rational verify.py independently certifies its displayed m=15/16 witness; numeric tests are not substitutes for the infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The area extremum of reduced thickness-one plane bodies is a motivated geometric problem. The result classifies the unique global area optimizer for a natural, nontrivial infinite-dimensional profile class extending a freshly studied source construction, rather than just recomputing a specific specimen. A certified area exceeding 0.79455604 improves a previously available constrained two-parameter bound of 0.78884379 and supplies new usable reduced-body examples; the strict stability identity adds quantitative structure.
